source.title: Probing Bias Formation in Medical LLMs through Activation Steering

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses mechanistic interpretability and reports experiments on SAE features and activation steering, but it does not test the claim versions about neuron-job shares, explanation accuracy on held-out activations, or neuron-based attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper's own measurements concern false-consensus bias representations and interventions in MedGemma-27B, not whether neurons have one or more nameable jobs. Its bias-mitigation and knowledge-retention results are not evidence for or against the listed claim versions. The zero-mitigation feature intervention and feature-overlap result are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study analyses SAE features and residual-stream steering for false-consensus sycophancy in MedGemma-27B. It never labels neuron jobs, estimates interpretable-neuron shares, scores explanations by simulation, or builds neuron attribution graphs. Its mentions of polysemanticity and superposition concern SAE features carrying a behavioural bias, not whether individual neurons are monosemantic. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that false-consensus sycophancy in MedGemma-27B is distributed and polymorphic: its direction is stable across layers while its feature substrate shifts, so sparse feature ablation fails. Layer-29 global steering reaches 21.9% mitigation with 91.2% retention. Cluster-conditioned steering reaches 29.2% mitigation but retention falls to 73%.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contrastive residual-stream differences, SAE feature analysis, and activation steering to study and mitigate false-consensus bias; it does not use the neuron explanation and validation procedure described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention outcome varies with layer depth, steering strength, and whether steering is global or cluster-conditioned.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating or subtracting the top-difference SAE features (notably feature 14444) at layers 27–28 gave zero percent bias mitigation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MedGemma-27B, false-consensus sycophancy is not removable by suppressing a few top SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-100 SAE feature overlap between adjacent layers is low (about 0.31–0.46, e.g. 33% for layers 26–27), while the cosine similarity of the dense bias direction stays high for layers 26–35.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A behaviourally defined bias direction can be geometrically stable across layers while the SAE features carrying it change.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting, Student Research Workshop)
record.problems: The analysis uses one model, one bias category, and a curated subset of 135 flip events. The paper states that generalization to other bias categories and clinical models remains to be tested. The reported results do not validate neuron explanations on held-out activations.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's global and cluster-conditioned steering mitigation and knowledge-retention rates, and its broader layer-sweep results, were left out because they evaluate interventions on false-consensus behavior rather than any listed claim version about neuron interpretability.

untested.parts: No neuron-pole job shares in Qwen3-32B.
No neuron-job shares across models or scales.
No analysis of canonical polysemantic neurons or recursive generalization.
No test of architecture, regularization or tool effects on interpretable-neuron share.
No neuron-based attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No held-out prediction test of explanations fitted to activating examples.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The authors call the bias 'polysemantic' and consistent with superposition. This refers to SAE features and a behavioural concept, not to neuron monosemanticity, so it does not bear on V1–V4. The study's single model and bias type are noted. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the share of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or jobs not yet understood in Qwen3-32B.
Does not compare neuron-job shares across models, architectures, or scales.
Does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not estimate interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized vision models or test architecture, regularization, or tool effects on those shares.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs built from model neurons or compare them with a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
Does not test whether neuron explanations fitted to activating examples predict activation on separate examples.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: MedGemma-27B
rows.operation_detail: Hard ablation and soft activation subtraction of the highest-difference SAE features
rows.note: The paper reports the result for targeted hard ablation and soft subtraction together; it does not give separate rates for the two interventions.
rows.check: Measures bias mitigation after ablating SAE features (not neurons). The state relative to any claim version cannot be determined. 'absent' describes the mitigation outcome, not a claim effect. Baseline is implicitly 0% mitigation (all 135 are flip events).

rows.subject: MedGemma-27B
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap of the top 100 SAE features carrying the largest activation differences across adjacent layers
rows.note: This is a feature-overlap measurement, not a measure of the share of neurons with particular jobs.
rows.check: Jaccard overlap of top-100 SAE features between layers 26 and 27 (33%). This is a feature-stability measure unrelated to neuron-job shares. The locator is Appendix B, Figure 5 (right panel).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
